selectedIssues.authoritativeDescription:
Audit: 14 September 2026. Confirmed on main `f089ea53239437fa0c4c27b4400326e686cb6083`; affected implementation also exists in published v0.1.4 (`12bb5a8effb8aebe77c6cfc4d8cd03d9bef45cdd`). Reproduce/fix from the current public maintenance baseline, then forward-port to 0.2.0. No production fix is included in this audit.

**Trigger and result.** The app cannot resolve its data directory, cannot read a durable launch/Steam verification marker, or finds invalid/conflicting maintenance state. It correctly refuses to start writers, but returns before constructing the window and emits its only explanation to stderr. A normal Explorer launch of the release Windows executable has no console, so the user sees an app that fails to open, with no visible diagnosis or safe recovery guidance.

**Source proof:** [lib.rs:614](<https://github.com/rndaom/execs/blob/f089ea53239437fa0c4c27b4400326e686cb6083/apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs#L614>) runs data-directory preflight, then on error calls `eprintln!` at line 621 and returns. [lib.rs:625](<https://github.com/rndaom/execs/blob/f089ea53239437fa0c4c27b4400326e686cb6083/apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs#L625>) does the same for restored maintenance state at lines 630–631. [restored_operation at line 457](<https://github.com/rndaom/execs/blob/f089ea53239437fa0c4c27b4400326e686cb6083/apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs#L457>) rejects unreadable, invalid, mismatched, or simultaneous markers. [main.rs:2](<https://github.com/rndaom/execs/blob/f089ea53239437fa0c4c27b4400326e686cb6083/apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs#L2>) selects the no-console Windows release subsystem. These are ordinary `Err` returns, so the panic logger does not record them.

**Acceptance criteria:** show an OS-native error before webview initialization, including the app's full diagnostic version and affected state path where available. Explain that the app stopped to protect the install and how to copy/report the error. Preserve the marker and fail-closed write behavior. Cover absent data-directory environment, corrupt/mismatched marker, access denial, multiple markers, and a successful normal startup. Do not automatically clear recovery markers to make the app open. Use isolated data directories for validation; this audit did not corrupt real user state.

Evidence bundle: `docs/audits/2026-09-14-project/backend-network.md`. Patch target 0.1.9; do not hold a serious fix for a milestone date. Add the user-facing \[Unreleased\] changelog line in the implementation commit.

selectedIssues.authoritativeDescription:
## Foundry implementation — September 22, 2026

Source audit and scoped overhead reductions are implemented in the current `rndaom/foundry-overhaul` working tree. This issue is **In Progress**, not Done: no new native TF2/PresentMon on/off traces were collected and causal contribution is still unclassified.

* The renderer lifecycle monitor previously made 1-second IPC reads and published equal state even while unfocused. It now retains immediate fail-closed boot/resume/post-operation reads, coalesces fresh follow-ups, ignores obsolete responses and preserves active leases; idle visible checks back off to 5 seconds, active leases use 1 second, failed reads back off to 30 seconds and hidden/unfocused periodic presentation checks pause.
* Native game write gates and the 1-second process-name monitor are unchanged. The write-lock renderer was already event-driven. Inventory was already single-flight and paused when hidden/inactive/busy/in-game.
* The bounded development Inventory helper now reads names-only sysinfo process data at its unchanged 100ms abort cadence instead of unnecessary default metadata. Its deadline/account/game guards are retained.
* Targeted lifecycle/Inventory/write-lock suites: **22 tests passed**; helper: **7 tests passed**, fmt and all-target Clippy passed. No runtime frame-time result is implied.
* Full timer/process/window inventory, source/thread distinctions, test evidence and a reproducible paired three-by-30-second PresentMon protocol are recorded in `docs/design/2026-09-22-overhaul/research/rnd-325-polling-audit.md`.

Remaining acceptance: run the actual candidate with TF2 foreground and both displays active; record normal/background priority and latency, paired on/off CSVs, periodic-stall comparison and independent-flip preservation; classify root cause/contribution/ruled-out or explicitly inconclusive. Keep <issue id="b16f386a-2ba2-4b3a-bfde-f94a7091cd53" href="https://linear.app/rndaom/issue/RND-324/make-the-execs-tf2-preload-hook-startup-safe">RND-324</issue>'s startup-hook capture separate. No version bump, release tag or publication is authorized.

---

## Context

During a Windows TF2 investigation, execs' companion process was running while periodic frame hitches were observed. The hitches sometimes aligned with roughly one-second process-check activity, so execs may add CPU/polling overhead or interact poorly with TF2's fullscreen/presentation state.

This is not proven to be the root cause: stopping `execs.exe` did not eliminate the stalls. With execs stopped, a 30-second capture still contained 19 CPU stalls over 20 ms totaling about 2.39 seconds, and TF2 remained on the separate AMD/DWM presentation failure path. The confirmed primary failure was the borderless/multi-monitor D3D9 presentation mode; this issue tracks the possible execs contribution.

## Scope

Audit the Windows execs background/process-monitoring path for high-frequency polling, process enumeration, window queries, priority, timers, and work performed on the UI or game-facing path.

## Acceptance criteria

* Identify every timer/poll interval and process/window query used by the Windows companion while TF2 is running.
* Replace unnecessary high-frequency polling with event-driven or backoff-based checks where practical.
* Ensure monitoring runs at normal/background priority and cannot block the UI, launch path, or profile/preloader transactions.
* Add a reproducible on/off benchmark using a short PresentMon capture with TF2 foreground and both displays active.
* Demonstrate that execs enabled versus disabled does not introduce periodic CPU stalls or degrade independent-flip presentation.
* Record the result explicitly as root cause, contributing factor, or ruled out; do not claim causation from correlation alone.

selectedIssues.authoritativeDescription:
## Context

TF2's execs preload hook is intentional: it preloads the user's configured mods before play. It is currently restored in the Steam launch options as:

`+exec overrides/execs_preload`

The hook is not the confirmed root cause of the recurring in-game FPS crawl, but its current startup sequence has unsafe side effects. The observed `tf/cfg/overrides/execs_preload.cfg` contains:

```
sv_pure -1
sv_allow_point_servercommand always
map itemtest
wait 10; disconnect
wait 1; clear
script_execute randommenumusic
```

The TF2 console log shows the hook entering `itemtest`, reporting that `itemtest.cfg` is absent, then shutting down the temporary server. This adds an unnecessary map/disconnect/clear sequence and can obscure real launch failures. It runs at startup, not every few seconds, so it does not alone explain the later recurring crawl.

## Scope

Keep mod preloading, but make the preload hook startup-safe, idempotent, and explicit about any temporary map/server work it requires. Separate actual mod/material preload from menu-music and cleanup side effects.

## Acceptance criteria

* `+exec overrides/execs_preload` remains supported and preloads the active profile's mods.
* Normal TF2 launch does not produce avoidable missing-`itemtest.cfg` warnings or an implicit map/disconnect/clear cycle.
* The hook runs once after TF2 initialization and cannot recursively or repeatedly re-enter itself.
* Failure is logged clearly without leaving TF2 in a temporary server or disconnected state.
* Validate with a clean launch and a short PresentMon capture; no regression to exclusive fullscreen/D3D9Ex independent-flip presentation.
* Preserve compatibility with existing profile-owned preloader selections and the 0.2.0 preloader work.
